newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air Canada Beaujolais Nouveau volumes double.
newsitem.headline: Air Canada Beaujolais Nouveau volumes double.

text.p: Air Canada said it expects this year's shipments of Beaujolais Nouveau to be double that of 1995.
"Last year we shipped around 60 tonnes of Beaujolais, whereas later this week, when our 1996 operation begins, we're banking on around 130 tonnes," Air Canada's director Daniel Bregere, told Reuters.

Increased demand in Canada for the young wine, a more successful sales and marketing campaign by the airline and the fact that Canadian Airlines had withdrawn its Paris-Toronto service, effective last month, were the main factors in Air Canada boosting its tonnage, Bregere said.
Air Canada will ship the vast majority of its Beaujolais Nouveau consignments over a three-day period aboard its daily Boeing 747 combi service from Paris to Montreal.
Smaller quantities will also be shipped on the Canadian carrier's four times weekly Paris-Toronto 767 passenger service.
"From our hubs at Montreal and Toronto we can serve the entire Canadian market," Bregere added.

Traditionally, airlines were able to drawing on the value-added quality of Beaujolais Nouveau, to negotiate tariffs well above standared rates but this has been tempered in recent years as the air cargo markets were hit by the recession and volumes were reduced as the wine lost some of its fashion appeal.

"France-Canada cargo rates have been subjected to downward pressures for a good part of 1996 and while there has been some relief since September, we'll be shipping Beaujolais Nouveau at more or less current market levels," Bregere said.
Custom dictates that Beaujolais Nouveau is available for consumption on the third Thursday of November, which this year falls on November 21.
